title: ooRexx implementation pitfalls learned in CivicPort
summary: CivicPort qualification exposed several ooRexx-specific traps that should be treated as durable project lessons: RESULT is special, instance variables need correct expose/attribute handling, parser/runtime wrapper types carry semantics, and message/class-side dispatch must be explicit.
invariants: Do not use ordinary local variable RESULT/result; message/function calls can clobber the special RESULT variable.
For non-attribute instance variables, use expose; do not write self~name = value unless an appropriate setter/attribute exists.
Do not invent a numeric coercion layer for ooRexx JSON values; preserve lexical/parser-native values exactly.
When a JSON schema requires string for numeric-looking data, retain/emit JsonString rather than converting it to a number.
Call class-side methods through the class, not through an instance.
In test Rexx, use call or assignment where a bare function-call expression could be parsed as a command.
procedure: Run rexxc over every src/*.cls before release.
Scan source/tests for accidental ordinary RESULT/result assignments.
Add regression tests whenever an ooRexx runtime semantic causes a real defect.

provenance.claim: JsonString preservation and no numeric/DateTime inference in current runtime surface.
All-source compilation and RESULT/result plus boundary static scans.
